supported: Brahe states that natal primary-direction year measures may use the Sun's actual DAILY motion with the corresponding arc of the equator.
Brahe argues for TRUE/UNEQUAL motion of Sun, Moon or other planets rather than abstract uniform motion.
In the meteorological/calendar example, Brahe instead uses the Moon's daily motion to define a different equatorial interval for each DAY; this must not be conflated with his natal convention.
not_supported_by_this_passage: No explicit definition of two enclosing LOCAL TRUE SOLAR MIDNIGHT timestamps appears in the inspected paragraph.
The precise equatorial epoch/nutation and TT/UT astronomical conventions of our SWIEPH implementation were not available in 1573.
The original 1573 page photograph was NOT inspected here; the Latin is a later critical transcription.
source_evidence_classes.interpretation: The 'Brahe midnight-to-midnight' 2009 Gansten reconstruction is computationally reproducible, but exact birth-day endpoints are NOT independently established from this 1573 source paragraph.
